transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-28
Time: 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus O'Connell (Redwood Partnerships), Aisha Khan (Galaxy Head of AI Partnerships), Ben Torres (Galaxy Solutions Architect), Lena Park (Galaxy Sales Director), Tom Wu (Galaxy Legal - listening in)

Summary: quick pipeline review and co-sell strategy, focused on three prioritized opportunities (two in fintech, one in health-tech). Discussed qualification criteria, technical blockers (VPC / data residency), pricing and margin split, playbook items, and next steps to enable Galaxy reps to co-sell. Decided to run lightweight benchmarks for one banking pilot and to draft a co-sell SOW + partner collateral.

Topics: co-sell motion, deal-specific technical constraints, onboarding timeline, enablement materials, legal/license ask, next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm jordan, i'll run the partner motion on our side. priya's our se. marcus is here for partnerships questions.
[00:08] Aisha Khan: hey jordan, thanks. aisha here — good to meet you all. we've got ben and lena on from ops and sales, tom's on the legal side.
[00:14] Jordan Lee: awesome, do you want to kick off with the pipeline? which deals are you most bullish on?
[00:20] Aisha Khan: sure. we have three we want to focus on. deal one is a mid-market neo-bank, looking for personalized financial guidance - fairly sensitive PII, they want on-prem options or strict VPC controls. deal two is a payments fraud product — less stringent residency but low latency required. deal three is a health-tech pilot with an employer benefits provider, high compliance and SOC2-ish.
[00:36] Ben Torres: quick note, for the neo-bank they're pushing legal to require KMS integration + full audit logs, and they asked about retention windows.
[00:42] Priya Nair: ok, from the tech side, we can do VPC private deployment, or dedicated capacity. KMS/HSM integrates. retention windows we can configure per-tenant; will need to confirm SLA on retention deletion.
[00:55] Lena Park: on the sales side, they want fast pricing — are we able to provide a co-sell margin table?
[01:02] Marcus O'Connell: yes we have a partner pricing model; jordan will send a draft. margin depends on dedicated vs hosted and committed capacity.
[01:10] Aisha Khan: timeline-wise, bank wants POC in 6 weeks if we can hit compliance answers.
[01:14] Jordan Lee: that is doable, we should prioritize the neo-bank then. priya, can we run a bench for their workload? what do you need?
[01:20] Priya Nair: i'll need sample prompt sets, expected qps, and sequence length distribution. for neo-bank, short prompts but many context tokens for transaction history, so kv-cache matters. also need to know if ddos/burst patterns expected.
[01:34] Ben Torres: we can share a sanitized sample and target qps — i'll send that after the call.
[01:38] Priya Nair: perfect. i'll give an estimate comparing hosted vs dedicated. note: dedicated gives consistent p99 latency and easier KMS integration; hosted is faster to spin up but multi-tenant and may have different retention defaults.
[01:52] Aisha Khan: regarding legal, they raised a few flags: encryption in transit + at rest, SOC2 evidence, and proof of data residency. can redwood provide SOC2 cert and region-specific deployment options?
[01:59] Jordan Lee: yes we are SOC2 compliant — i will attach our compliance pack. we support region pinning and private deployments. we'll include the security playbook link after the call.
[02:09] Tom Wu: two small legal items — we need to see the data processing addendum and indemnity language for co-sell. is that something you have a template for?
[02:16] Marcus O'Connell: we have a partner DPA and co-sell template, jordan will share, but we'll need to redline for enterprise specifics.
[02:22] Lena Park: for pricing, the bank is focused on predictable unit economics. do you have batching/quantization recommendations to lower cost?
[02:29] Priya Nair: yes. for their pattern i recommend prefix caching and model quantization profile; we can demo numbers. the optimizer tool suggests settings by workload — i'll include a short config.
[02:40] Ben Torres: is there a recommended fallback if capacity is constrained? i.e., degrade to smaller model automatically?
[02:45] Jordan Lee: yes, we support smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants. can define policy per-deal to prioritize latency vs cost.
[02:52] Aisha Khan: great. for the fraud payments deal, latency is critical. that might favor dedicated or reserved burst capacity, right?
[02:58] Priya Nair: correct, dedicated pool with autoscaling and burst helps keep p50/p95 low. or host in the same region and set higher priority routing.
[03:06] Aisha Khan: any competitor asks that come up from customers?
[03:09] Jordan Lee: some ask about OpenAI for accuracy and some about Anthropic on safety — we position Redwood as production-first, cost-aware and flexible deployment. we should prepare collateral comparing typical cost per thousand tokens and latency tradeoffs.
[03:24] Lena Park: for enablement, can you provide a one-pager for reps and a playbook with typical objections? also ideally a short demo script.
[03:32] Marcus O'Connell: yes we have a partner playbook template; jordan will adapt with Galaxy branding and send.
[03:38] Ben Torres: technical Q - does private deployment still allow Redwood Console observability? we need per-route logs and token-level cost breakdown for showback.
[03:46] Priya Nair: yes, private control plane optionally sends telemetry to customer or to Redwood with RBAC. we can configure retention and what flows to the console.
[03:55] Aisha Khan: on the big health-tech pilot, they asked about model evals and regression alerts. do you tie evals to webhook notifications?
[04:02] Priya Nair: we support quality monitoring, can set eval sets and alert on regressions; webhook actions are supported to trigger rollbacks or notify Slack.
[04:11] Jordan Lee: ok, circling back, action items — jordan will send playbook and partner pricing, priya will run benchmarks for the neo-bank workload, ben will provide sanitized samples and architecture notes. aisha to route intros to champions.
[04:22] Aisha Khan: yep we'll do that. also quick ask — can you prepare a short statement of work example that we can share with their procurement?
[04:29] Jordan Lee: yes will draft an SOW and co-sell revenue share examples.
[04:33] Lena Park: one more — any red flags on support SLAs? bank requires 24/7 support for launch week and a named escalation contact.
[04:40] Marcus O'Connell: we can provide enhanced onboarding support as part of the co-sell bundle for an initial period and assign an escalation owner. we'll document that in the SOW.
[04:49] Tom Wu: regarding indemnities, we'll review the template but expect some negotiation on liability caps.
[04:53] Jordan Lee: understood. we'll mark legal items for redline and aim to keep standard limits unless the customer pushes hard.
[04:58] Priya Nair: technical note — for the neo-bank, if there's a hard requirement for no outbound internet from the model host, we might need on-prem package; that's a different procurement timeline.
[05:08] Ben Torres: good point, i'll check with the bank if they require air-gapped.
[05:11] Jordan Lee: ok moving to deal sequencing — propose we run the neo-bank POC first (6 weeks), fraud payments as second (4-6 week pilot), and health pilot after we close the first two. everyone ok?
[05:20] Aisha Khan: yes that's the internal priority.
[05:23] Marcus O'Connell: i'll coordinate enablement sessions for Galaxy reps — maybe a 30 minute live training + recorded demo.
[05:29] Jordan Lee: sounds good. next meeting week of 9/8 to review benchmarks and early pipeline updates.
[05:33] Lena Park: will attend.
[05:35] Ben Torres: will share sample artifacts by end of day Thursday.
[05:38] Jordan Lee: perfect. thanks everyone.
[05:41] Aisha Khan: thanks all, talk soon.

Notes: shared artifacts references — playbook template (link: /shared/partner-playbook-galaxy.pdf), pricing spreadsheet (link: /shared/galaxy-pricing-draft.xlsx), compliance pack (link: /shared/redwood-soc2-2025.pdf).

Action items (in transcript): Jordan - send playbook, SOW draft, pricing sheet; Priya - benchmarks and config recommendations; Ben - sanitized prompt samples + architecture notes; Aisha - intros to champions.

End of transcript.
